modifications.problem: Date column stored as object string, not datetime
modifications.impact: Temporal analyses (trend, seasonality, time‑based splits) require proper datetime type; mis‑typed dates cause ordering errors and faulty feature engineering.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Convert Date to pandas datetime using `pd.to_datetime(errors='coerce')`; any unparsable entries (expected <0.1% if any) will be flagged for manual review.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Leave as string (would break time series), drop rows with unparsable dates (unnecessary data loss).
modifications.effect: All 100% of rows, column Date type changed from object to datetime64[ns]; at most a handful of rows may become NaT for manual correction.

modifications.impact: Age is critical for demographic segmentation and for any model that conditions on customer profile; systematic missingness could bias results if not handled properly.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing Age using median age within the same StoreLocation + ProductCategory group (fallback to overall median if group size < 30). This respects locality‑specific demographics while avoiding over‑fitting.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Mean imputation (sensitive to outliers), simple overall median (ignores geographical/product differences), dropping rows (would lose 20% of data), predictive regression model (adds complexity and risk of leakage).
modifications.effect: Approximately 20% of rows (those with missing Age) will have their Age value replaced by a group‑median figure.

modifications.impact: Amount drives revenue calculations and downstream profit/loss modeling; missing amounts distort total sales and per‑transaction metrics.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing Amount using median transaction amount for the same ProductCategory + StoreLocation combination (fallback to overall median if insufficient records). This leverages product‑price expectations per store.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Mean imputation (skewed by high‑value purchases), dropping rows (loss of 10% data), predictive regression (risk of leakage, added model bias).
modifications.effect: All rows with missing Amount (≈10% of dataset) receive a group‑median amount value.

modifications.impact: FeedbackScore is used for satisfaction modeling; missing scores can bias average rating calculations and affect model training if not addressed.
modifications.strategy_chosen: Impute missing FeedbackScore with the median score of the same StoreLocation + ProductCategory, reflecting local service/product perception; fallback to overall median if group too small.
modifications.alternatives_rejected: Mean imputation (sensitive to extreme ratings), mode imputation (ignores rating scale), predictive model (complex, risk of over‑fitting), row removal (data loss).
modifications.effect: Rows where FeedbackScore is missing (≈10%) will be filled with the calculated group median.

restricted_columns.TransactionID: restricted - primary key, must never be altered or dropped

data_integrity.validation_result: The repaired dataset retains all original transactional records, with Date correctly typed, Age, Amount, and FeedbackScore sensibly imputed using context‑aware group medians, and no changes to primary key or outcome columns; thus it faithfully represents the original sales process while being ready for analysis.

anomalies: Age missing in ~20% of rows – potential bias if missingness is systematic
Amount and FeedbackScore each missing in ~10% – could weaken revenue and satisfaction models
Amount distribution highly right‑skewed with max 899 vs median 120 – indicates possible high‑value outliers
IsReturned only 2 returns (20%) – low event rate may limit predictive power

target_associations.IsReturned: Low prevalence (20% returns); weak relationships observed with Age and Amount (not shown in correlation matrix), suggesting need for additional predictors such as ProductCategory or StoreLocation for reliable return prediction.
target_associations.FeedbackScore: Moderate negative correlation with Amount (-0.33) and slight positive correlation with Age (+0.20); indicates higher spenders rate experience slightly lower, while older shoppers tend to give higher scores.
target_associations.Amount: Negatively correlated with FeedbackScore (-0.33) and modestly negatively with Age (-0.28); higher transaction values are linked to lower satisfaction and younger customers.
